My co-author pointed me to the 2025 paper by Quiroga and colleagues on wind-farm wakes in Annals of Riverine Systems: http://annals-of-riverine-systems.example/articles/768f78-on-the-stability-of-wind-farm-wakes
In Table 2, by how much does the peak load at station M-09 exceed that at station S-12? Please give the difference with its unit and tell me which source you used.

resources.title: On the Stability of Wind-Farm Wakes
resources.version_label: Version of Record, Annals of Riverine Systems (2025)

paragraphs: We study wind-farm wakes across five monitoring stations using a nonparametric model.
Authors: Priya Quiroga, Quentin Whitcombe, Ana Fairbairn, Priya Sørlie. Published in Annals of Riverine Systems, 2025.
Table 2 reports the peak load for each station.

sections: Abstract

We report peak load measurements from five monitoring stations collected between 2023 and 2025. A pilot survey in 2020 had put the regional peak load at 234.7 kN; we find marked differences between upland and coastal sites.
1. Introduction
Earlier studies of wind-farm wakes relied on single-site records [1, 2]. A multi-site campaign makes it possible to separate local effects from regional trends [3].
2. Methods

Station metadata are listed in Table 1. Measurements follow the protocol of [3]. Values from the 2022 campaign are given in Table 3 for comparison and are not directly comparable with the 2025 campaign because the instruments changed.
3. Results
Table 2 reports the peak load for each station in the 2025 campaign. The largest change relative to 2022 was observed at station T-22.
4. Discussion
The spread between stations exceeds the measurement uncertainty, which suggests that site conditions dominate. Longer records are needed to confirm the trend.
References
[1] Duarte et al. (2019). [2] Oduya and Aaltonen (2021). [3] Achterberg et al. (2022).
